title: Automations: the build plan, one piece at a time

steps.intro: The job: "Every morning at 8, check my spending and email me if anything looks off." Reads the Money page (Always allowed), sends email (Asks first), OpenRouter, $5 a month.

steps.path: A chat, or Automations → New automation
steps.headline: You make it from a chat or with New automation; Create saves it switched on.
steps.changed: In a chat, the assistant fills in the short check popup; Turn on saves it. Nothing runs before that.
steps.notice: Checked by: you, in the dev window. Ask a chat, press Turn on, see the card appear.

steps.headline: At 8:00 it starts by itself, with no chat opening, as long as YouCoded is open.
steps.changed: If the computer was off at 8:00, the job's Missed runs setting decides: run once when it wakes, skip, or run differently. Three missed mornings make one run, not three.
steps.notice: Checked by: a test with a pretend clock. At 8:00 exactly one run starts; three days later, exactly one run.

steps.path: The run reads the Money page
steps.headline: Things set to Always allowed just happen; anything not on the job's list is refused.
steps.changed: Reading the Money page goes through. Another website or a command it wasn't given is refused, because new jobs start with both "Other" settings at Never.
steps.notice: Checked by: a test where a pretend assistant tries one allowed and one unlisted thing.

steps.path: The run wants to send an email
steps.headline: Something set to Asks first pauses the run, notifies you and puts the job under Waiting for you.
steps.changed: A notification on your computer and phone, the orange dot on the Pages button, and the job moves to the top group. Closing the app keeps it waiting.
steps.notice: Checked by: tests that the run stops at that step, shows Waiting, and is still waiting after a restart.

steps.headline: Allow carries on, Don't allow skips that step, and no answer in time does what the job says.
steps.changed: "Wait up to" ends with: skip that step, stop the run, or do something else you wrote.
steps.notice: Checked by: one test per choice, and you clicking a real notification once in the dev window.

steps.headline: A finished run is kept under its job with its whole conversation, and never shows among your chats.
steps.changed: One box per run: when, result, cost, what it did, Open conversation (read-only). Not in your chat list, Resume, chat search or the phone's chat list. Last 50 kept.
steps.notice: Checked by: a test that after a run nothing new appears in any of those lists.

steps.headline: At the limit the run stops before its next step and shows Limit reached with the real amount.
steps.changed: The step already going finishes, so it can end a few cents over. A Claude job has no limit and shows tokens used instead.
steps.notice: Checked by: a test at 3¢ a step against 10¢ that must stop after step 4 at 12¢, and you trying a real 1¢ limit.

steps.page: Where it plugs into the app
steps.intro: Every place outside the Automations page that changes. Anything not listed here stays exactly as it is.

steps.headline: The Pages button gets an orange dot while any automation is waiting for you.
steps.changed: It goes away once nothing is waiting.
steps.notice: Same dot on the job's page in the Pages list.

steps.headline: A page's Settings lists that page's automations with their switches and Open in Automations.
steps.changed: Only jobs that belong to that page.

steps.headline: A page can have a button that runs one of its own automations, with a spinner and a waiting dot.
steps.changed: The page kit draws the spinner and dot, so they look the same on every page. A page can also say "something happened" to start its own jobs.
steps.notice: Checked by: you, pressing the Money page's check button in the dev window.

steps.headline: In any chat, the assistant can offer to turn a request into an automation.
steps.changed: It opens the approved check popup. Works in Claude chats and ChatGPT / OpenRouter chats alike.
steps.notice: The assistant only offers it when you ask for something repeated or scheduled.

steps.headline: YouCoded starts sending system notifications, which it has never done before.
steps.changed: Only for automations: needs you, has news, failed, each switchable per job. Clicking one opens the job.
steps.notice: Your computer may ask once whether to allow YouCoded notifications.

steps.headline: Reused as they are: the model picker, your Claude, ChatGPT and OpenRouter connections, the assistant's tools and safety rules.
steps.changed: Untouched: your chats, chat list, Resume, chat search and sync.
steps.notice: A job gets the same tools a chat gets, with its own permissions on top.

steps.page: Rules I filled in without asking you
steps.intro: Your answers didn't cover these, so I picked. Each is easy to change now, harder after the build.

steps.path: Permissions → Other websites / Other commands and files
steps.headline: What should a new job do with a website or command you didn't list?
steps.today: Each job lists what it may do. Two settings cover everything else.
steps.problem: The default decides what a job does on day one, before you have tuned it.
steps.proposal: Pick the starting setting for new jobs; you can still change it per job.

options.label: Never
pros: Nothing happens you didn't list.
Matches "and that's it" from your answer.
cons: A job may fail its first run until you add what it needs.

options.label: Asks first
pros: The first run shows you what it wanted.

steps.headline: How should a new job handle an Asks first step, before you change anything?
steps.today: Each job chooses: wait for you (up to a time, then skip, stop or do something else) or skip and continue.
steps.problem: A new job needs a starting point.
steps.proposal: Pick the default for new jobs.

options.label: Wait until next run
options.summary: Waits until its next scheduled time, then skips that step.
pros: Gives you the most time to answer.
Never piles up two waiting runs.
cons: A daily job may hold an answer for a whole day.

options.label: Wait an hour
options.summary: Waits an hour, then skips that step.
pros: Runs finish the same morning.
cons: Miss the notification for an hour and it's gone.

options.label: Skip and continue
pros: Never waits on you.
cons: Anything set to Asks first effectively never happens unless you Run now.

steps.headline: What should a new job do about runs missed while the computer was off?
steps.today: Each job picks: run once when the computer wakes, skip them, or run differently.
steps.problem: A new job needs a starting point.
steps.proposal: Pick the default for new jobs.

options.label: Run once on wake
pros: A morning check still happens if you opened the laptop at 10.
cons: It may run at a time you didn't expect.

options.label: Skip them
pros: Runs only ever happen at their set time.
cons: A laptop that's often asleep at 8 never runs its 8:00 job.

steps.headline: Which notifications should a new job start with?
steps.today: Three switches per job: needs you, has news, failed.
steps.problem: Too many and you mute them; too few and you miss a waiting job.
steps.proposal: Pick which start on; each job can change them.

options.label: Needs you
pros: Without it a waiting job sits unseen.

options.label: Has news
pros: You hear when it found something.
cons: A chatty job can notify daily.

options.label: Failed
pros: You learn a job broke.
cons: A flaky internet morning sends one.

steps.headline: How many automations may run at the same time?
steps.today: Nothing runs in the background yet.
steps.problem: Many at once slows the computer and spends faster; one at a time makes a long job hold up the rest.
steps.proposal: Pick a number; the rest wait their turn.

options.label: Two
pros: A long job doesn't block a quick one.
The computer stays responsive.
cons: A third due job starts late.

options.label: One
pros: Lightest on the computer.
cons: One slow job delays all the others.

options.label: No limit
pros: Everything starts on time.
cons: Eight jobs at 8:00 can slow everything down.

steps.path: A job is due while its last run is still going
steps.headline: When a job is due but its last run hasn't finished, what happens?
steps.today: Nothing runs in the background yet.
steps.problem: Two copies of the same job could do the same thing twice, like send two emails.
steps.proposal: Pick what the new due time does.

options.label: Skip it
pros: Never does the same thing twice.
cons: A run is lost if the last one was stuck.

options.label: Run after
options.summary: Starts as soon as the last run ends.
pros: No run is lost.
cons: A slow job falls further and further behind.

steps.path: Changing a setting while it runs
steps.headline: When you change a job's settings while it's running, when does the change apply?
steps.today: Settings save as you change them.
steps.problem: Changing permissions halfway could surprise a run that is already doing things.

options.label: Next run
pros: A run behaves the same from start to end.
cons: Removing a permission doesn't stop a run already using it; you'd pause the job.

options.label: Right away
pros: Taking away a permission takes effect at once.

steps.headline: Pages may start only their own automations, never another page's or a standalone one. Right?
steps.today: Jobs belong to a page or stand alone.
steps.problem: A page from someone else (later, with sharing) could otherwise run your jobs.
steps.proposal: Yes keeps pages to their own jobs. No lets any page start any job you allow it.

steps.path: Deleting a page that has automations
steps.headline: When you delete a page that has automations, what happens to them?
steps.today: Deleting a page moves it to history, where Put back restores it.
steps.problem: Its jobs could keep running with nothing to report to.
steps.proposal: Pick what happens to its jobs.

options.label: Ask me
options.summary: The delete popup asks: delete them too, or keep them standalone.
pros: Nothing disappears by surprise.

options.label: Pause them
options.summary: Kept and paused; Put back turns them on again.
pros: No extra question.
Put back is complete.
cons: Paused jobs pile up in Automations.

steps.path: A Claude job waiting when the app closes
steps.headline: A waiting Claude job can't resume where it was after a restart. Restart it from its notes instead?
steps.today: ChatGPT and OpenRouter jobs pick up exactly where they paused. Claude's background mode can't, because the run isn't saved as a chat.
steps.problem: A Claude job waiting for you when you close YouCoded would otherwise be lost.
steps.proposal: Yes: it starts again with what it had done so far, and the run says "picked up after restart". No: the run ends as Stopped and the next scheduled run starts fresh.

steps.path: A Claude job when Claude can't apply its permissions
steps.headline: If an update to Claude ever stops it applying a job's permissions, the run fails instead of running unprotected. Right?
steps.today: Claude jobs rely on Claude's own background mode to respect the job's list.
steps.problem: If that mode changes, a job could run with more freedom than you gave it.
steps.proposal: Yes: the run fails with a clear reason until YouCoded is updated. No: it runs anyway with Claude's normal limits.

steps.headline: Each device runs its own automations, not synced, for this version. OK?
steps.today: Pages and chats sync between your devices; automations would be new.
steps.problem: Syncing jobs means deciding which device runs them, or both would run each one.
steps.proposal: Yes: each device has its own list for now, and syncing comes later. No: syncing becomes part of this build, which adds a "runs on" setting per job and more time.

steps.page: From your answers, and anything else
steps.intro: Already decided on earlier decks; here so the whole plan is in one place.

steps.headline: From your answers: $5 default limit, finish the step then stop, last 50 runs kept, and per-job approvals, missed runs and notifications.
steps.changed: Also not in this version: starting when something happens elsewhere (needs step 5's sign-ins), chains of jobs (waits on plans), and running while YouCoded is closed.
